title: Why Your First $1,000 Is So Hard to Save

scenes.voice: Your first one thousand dollars can feel impossible to save. And it's not always because you spend too much.
scenes.headline: WHY IS THE FIRST $1,000 SO HARD?

scenes.voice: Payday hits. For a moment, your bank balance looks amazing.
scenes.headline: PAYDAY HITS 💸

scenes.voice: Then rent, groceries, subscriptions, and bills show up like they were waiting outside.
scenes.headline: THEN… THE BILLS ARRIVE

scenes.voice: One surprise expense, like a car repair or a dentist visit, can wipe out what you set aside.
scenes.headline: SURPRISE EXPENSE: $240

scenes.voice: Try this: move a small amount to savings automatically on payday. Start with ten or twenty dollars. Make it easy to repeat.
scenes.headline: AUTOMATE A SMALL AMOUNT

scenes.voice: Your first thousand isn't built in one perfect month. It's built one repeatable payday at a time. Follow The Money Stickman for money lessons that make sense.
scenes.headline: ONE PAYDAY AT A TIME.

notes: Illustrative example only. No guaranteed results. Do not imply that $1,000 is equally attainable for everyone; encourage viewers to adapt savings to their circumstances.
